entries.chain: Any EVM chain, Solana, and more
entries.description: The open, HTTP-native payment standard. A server answers an unpaid request with 402 Payment Required, the client pays in crypto, the server serves the resource.
entries.fees: Zero protocol fees; network gas separate
entries.name: x402

entries.description: An open protocol for agent payments built on signed, verifiable mandates (intent, cart, payment) that prove the user authorized the agent to pay for a specific purchase. Specification v0.2, donated to the FIDO Alliance.
entries.fees: Not published (open protocol, not a priced service)
entries.name: Google AP2 - Agent Payments Protocol
entries.run_by: Originated by Google with 60+ organizations; now with the FIDO Alliance

entries.description: An open protocol that lets agents pay for API services, designed rail-agnostic so different payment networks can implement it. Settles on Tempo.
entries.fees: Not published
entries.name: MPP - Machine Payments Protocol

entries.asset: ERC-20 tokens on EVM networks; SPL tokens on Solana
entries.chain: Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Monad, World, Solana, and more
entries.description: Coinbase's hosted x402 service that verifies signed payments and settles them onchain, so a seller runs no settlement infrastructure of its own.
entries.fees: First 1,000 onchain transactions a month free, then $0.001 each; verification always free; gas separate
entries.name: Coinbase CDP x402 Facilitator

entries.description: Wever Labs' MCP-accessible money toolkit: paid tools and commerce rails settled in USDC on Base via x402. Main endpoint answers live with 57 tools, plus 13 more across dedicated split, conditional, and invoice endpoints and 6 on the money-back endpoint.
entries.fees: 10 free calls per wallet per rolling 30 days; then 0.10 USDC per call for most tools, 1.00 for diligenceops-paid-run, 0.25 for daily-operator-brief, 2.00 per delegated-authority mandate
entries.name: Wever Pay / Wever Labs MCP

entries.description: Locks USDC in a Base escrow contract, releases in full at a release time or on the named approver's approval, refunds in full to the payer after the deadline. Payer-only cancel before release.
entries.fees: 0.10 USDC per call under the shared 10 free calls per wallet per rolling 30 days; maximum 300 USDC per payment
entries.name: Wever conditional payments / escrow

entries.description: Splits one USDC payment across 2 to 32 recipients in a single atomic execution, by percentage or fixed amounts.
entries.fees: 0.10 USDC per call under the shared 10 free calls per wallet per rolling 30 days; maximum 300 USDC per split
entries.name: Wever split payments

entries.description: Creates shareable USDC invoices that an agent or human pays once via x402. Paid invoices keep their completed status. One payment authorization per invoice.
entries.fees: 0.10 USDC per call under the shared 10 free calls per wallet per rolling 30 days; maximum invoice 300 USDC
entries.name: Wever invoicing

entries.description: Opens a dispute over a funded escrow or work order, pauses release and refund, both sides submit evidence, and the operator signs a release, refund, or split decision. Unresolved funds return to the payer after 14 days.
entries.fees: 0.10 USDC per call; limit 25 USDC per case and 100 USDC resolved per UTC day
entries.name: Wever dispute resolution rail

entries.chain: Arbitrum, Arc, Avalanche, Base, Ethereum, Monad, Optimism, Polygon PoS, Unichain
entries.description: Policy-controlled agent wallets to hold and spend USDC, per-request x402 payments, gas-free nanopayments, and a marketplace to discover payable services.
entries.fees: Gas $0 (sponsored) on agent-wallet transactions; swap provider fee 2 bps; Gateway protocol fee 0.5 bps on cross-chain x402 payments, free same-chain; nanopayments down to $0.000001
entries.name: Circle Agent Stack

entries.chain: Fiat card and bank rails; stablecoin acceptance
entries.description: Agent Toolkit (MCP server, skills, CLI) plus the Agentic Commerce Suite for merchants selling through agents, on Stripe's fiat and stablecoin rails.
entries.fees: Standard card processing 2.9% + 30 cents per successful domestic card transaction; stablecoin acceptance 1.5%; dispute fee $15.00
entries.name: Stripe for AI agents

entries.chain: Base, Solana, Polygon (x402); fiat via Stripe, PayPal/Braintree, Visa card delegation
entries.description: Payments and monetization for AI agents: metering, pricing plans, access control, and settlement, including delegated card spending via x402.
entries.fees: Check directly; their own published pages differ (1% vs 1% to 2%)
entries.name: Nevermined

entries.asset: USD stablecoins (TIP-20); gas paid in stablecoins
entries.description: A payments-first Layer 1 built for stablecoin payments, global payouts, agentic payments, and enterprise settlement. MPP is its companion open standard.
entries.fees: Not published
entries.name: Tempo

entries.description: Originally an x402 API-monetization product; now a platform for deploying secure, auditable agents with organizational guardrails. Its x402 payments docs and API remain live.
entries.fees: Not published
entries.name: Corbits

entries.description: The agent trust stack: verified Know Your Agent (KYA) identity plus an agentic wallet and checkout so agents can access sites, log in, and pay on a user's behalf.
entries.fees: Not published
entries.name: Skyfire

entries.description: An Ethereum draft standard giving agents portable onchain identity (an ERC-721 NFT), a reputation registry for client feedback, and a validation registry for independent checks of completed work. Payments are deliberately out of scope.
entries.fees: None (the standard defines no fees; ordinary gas only)
entries.name: ERC-8004 - Trustless Agents
entries.run_by: Open Ethereum EIP, no single company

entries.description: An official ENS standard that lets an ENS name verifiably link to an AI agent registered in an onchain registry such as ERC-8004, using a single text record. ENS itself is general naming infrastructure, not an agent product.
entries.fees: Not published (no agent-specific pricing)
entries.name: ENS for agents (ENSIP-25)

entries.description: Opens Visa's payment network to AI agents so they can find, shop, and buy on a consumer's behalf using tokenized AI-Ready Cards, with consumer-set spending limits and transaction controls.
entries.fees: Not published
entries.name: Visa Intelligent Commerce

entries.asset: Fiat; Agent Pay for Machines settles in fiat or stablecoins
entries.chain: Card network; Agent Pay for Machines settles via Base
entries.description: Tokenized payment credentials (Agentic Tokens) that let AI agents buy on behalf of consumers and businesses within approved limits. Agent Pay for Machines extends this to agents paying other agents and services for digital services over x402.
entries.fees: Not published
entries.name: Mastercard Agent Pay

entries.description: A marketplace where AI agents list services and hire each other, paying on delivery through escrow smart contracts or instant pay-per-call (A2MCP) transactions under one shared onchain identity.
entries.fees: No service fees currently; users pay gas and third-party protocol fees; providers set their own prices
entries.name: OKX AI Agent Marketplace (A2MCP)

entries.chain: Base, Base Sepolia, Solana, Solana Devnet
entries.description: The discovery layer for x402: a machine-readable catalog of payable HTTP endpoints and MCP tools that agents can search, then pay for and call.
entries.fees: Listing is free; services set their own per-call prices, paid via x402
entries.name: x402 Bazaar

entries.description: An open standard that lets AI applications connect to external data sources, tools, and workflows through one interface. The agent-to-tool layer, not a payment rail.
entries.fees: None (open protocol)
entries.name: MCP - Model Context Protocol
entries.run_by: Originated by Anthropic; now with the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation

entries.description: An open standard for agent-to-agent communication: agents discover each other via Agent Cards, delegate tasks, and share results. AP2 is designed as an extension of A2A. The agent-to-agent layer, not a payment rail.
entries.fees: None (open protocol)
entries.name: A2A - Agent2Agent Protocol
entries.run_by: Originated by Google; now with the Linux Foundation
